comments.body:
🤖 **Not actionable as a code PR — this is an experiment-comparison task.**

This issue tracks a matched-quality comparison of the H100 mixture-swap ladder against the #8435 baseline and a human proceed/defer decision on Monday's data swap. Every checklist item (matched held-out loss / bits-per-byte, benchmark results, scaling fits, gradient-norm and token-drop stability, the swap decision) requires live W&B runs, cluster checkpoints, and human judgment on a production run. None maps to a source change, so I am not opening a PR.

Two concrete repo notes for whoever runs the comparison:

- The mixture weights `best_mixture_996f489106c7b922.json`, described as sitting beside [`launch_h100_scaling_ladder.py`](experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/launch_h100_scaling_ladder.py), are not in the tree. Publishing them with the comparison (per the description) needs the launch-time source data, which is not reconstructable from the repo.
- d1024 and d1536 had not finished at last check and d1536 had not reached its 25% switch, so any scaling fit before Monday extrapolates from partial rungs — mark that uncertainty in the report.

If a specific automatable slice emerges (for example, committing the pinned launcher revision and mixture weights, or a script that pulls the matched W&B metrics), point me at it and I will take that piece.

comments.body:
🤖 d1536 finished all 90,767 updates and its final evaluation: **2.54317 macro loss / 0.91844 BPB**, or **1.20× compute-equivalent speedup** over the old ladder at equal throughput. BPB improves on 15/16 subsets; Wikipedia regresses by 0.50%.

The issue summary and [per-subset plots](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/h100-mix25-paloma/final-2026.09.15.1/index.html) now use measured finals. The prior adjusted forecast was 2.54351 loss / 0.91867 BPB (1.19×).
